uncertainties.detail: Family Bahri is explicitly a collective family label rather than a natural person. Schema v8 has no family record type, and no reliable source establishes that the label denotes one continuing legal entity, so unresolved_placeholder is the appropriate terminal classification rather than person or institution.

SuperYacht Times material preserved by Nautipedia and a later secondary account directly connect Majestic M to the Bahri family of Lebanon. Burgess independently identifies the 1979 buyer only as a Middle Eastern family. These sources support the collective association but do not name a natural person, family branch, trust or company.

The input dates the historical relationship from June 1976 to 1987. Public sources place delivery in 1978, a Burgess sale to a Middle Eastern family in 1979 and Petter Sundt's acquisition in 1987. The 1976 date may reflect the build process, but the reviewed sources do not prove an acquisition date and no chronology correction is proposed.

The historical SuperYacht Times account says the vessel was built for the Bahri family, while YachtBuyer's build story describes an initial British property-developer project and a later unnamed Greek-based owner who died. Both may describe different stages, but neither supplies the legal owner sequence needed to reconcile them.

The Bahri Group's own site describes a late Lebanese founder, Alaeddine Bahri, who built an oil-trading and shipping business later managed by his sons. The surname, country, era and maritime sector make this a plausible lead, not an identity bridge. No source reviewed connects the group or any relative to Majestic M, so its facts are not assigned to the owner record.

Lebanese nationality and Lebanon residence are compatible with the yacht-history attribution, but Dead mortality status cannot describe a multigenerational family. Gender, birth and death fields are likewise inapplicable without a named natural person. Unresolved-placeholder rules prohibit person-detail proposals, so the mismatch is recorded without a correction.

Oil trading and shipping describe the plausible Bahri Group branch, but its connection to person ID 196 is unproved. Founder, successor and family-shareholder relationships would also vary by generation. Creation industry, current primary industry, origin and current relationship therefore remain Unknown rather than converting a surname match into wealth findings.
